title: Web application architecture
goal: Show a scalable web application request path and asynchronous worker tier.

rubric.must: Browser Client, CDN/WAF, and Load Balancer visibly form the entry request path.
The load balancer visibly fans out to two separate app-server blocks.
Both app servers visibly connect to the cache and database.
A job queue visibly feeds two workers, both of which connect to the database.
HTTPS, SQL, cache, and job-message labels are visible on relevant paths.

ideal.notes: Drawn by `scripts/visual-eval/draw-blockdiagram-target.mjs`, which draws all eight cases from one kit so the set is one drawing repeated. A functional block diagram of Web Application Architecture. 10 blocks carry the forward signal path. Every wire is orthogonal, every arrowhead lands on a block edge, signal names are set in italic beside the wire they name, and a legend at the foot states the line codes. Drawn in the idiom of the block-diagram exemplar (`visual-eval/exemplars/blockdiagram/ideal.svg`): ink outlines, block labels at 13 over at most two lines, signal names in italic slate beside the wire they name, a 34 px summing junction with its signs set just outside the circle, a filled dot at every pickoff, orthogonal wires only, and terracotta spent on nothing but the measured/feedback path. A long chain is folded into bands joined by a labelled channel, the exemplar's own solution to a chain too long for one row. One extension of the exemplar: each block body carries a pale fill keyed to the `role:` the DSL declares for it — input, control, actuator, plant, sensor, output — with a swatch legend at the foot. The exemplar leaves every body white, which discards information the author supplied on every single block; the fills are kept pale and the outlines ink so terracotta remains the loudest thing on the page and still means only one thing. Routing picks whichever corner misses every other block, and the checker tests each label against every other label, every block body, every wire segment and the canvas edge, plus every wire against every block body: 0 overlaps and no wire runs through a block.
